raw_response:
I have farmed this land for 60 years. I never went to school, but I know every ridge in these fields. My father showed me how to hold the plough, and I learned the rest by watching what works and copying the men in the village who always have a full barn.

I have 10.2 mu. I plant wheat on 9.5 mu in the autumn, and after we cut the wheat in June, I put maize on that same 9.5 mu. The other 0.7 mu near the well I keep for stevia. My wife and I are the only ones in the house now, so when the wheat must come off and the corn must go in during the same hot week, I hire two young men from the village for three days. If you miss that window, the corn will not ripen before frost.

For the wheat, I plough the field deep after the maize stalks are cleared. I buy the improved wheat seed from the shop in town — the same kind Old Zhang uses, the one in the red bag. Before sowing, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu; those are 50-jin bags, the ones with three numbers on the front. In the spring, when the wheat starts to turn green, I topdress with 40 jin of urea on each mu. Fertilizer is dear — a bag of compound is 160 yuan and urea is 120 yuan now — but I would rather spend the money than see the wheat go yellow. A bad harvest means buying grain to eat, and that is a disaster; wasting a handful of fertilizer is just a cost. I water three times with the well pump: once before winter so the cold does not kill it, once when the stems shoot up, and once when the grain is filling in the heads. I spray pesticide twice — once when the aphids come, and once for that white dust on the leaves. If the wind and rain treat us fair, I expect 550 jin of wheat per mu.

For the summer maize, I plant hybrid seed right after the wheat harvest. Everyone buys hybrid now because the old seed does not grow the same anymore. There is no time to plough, so I plant directly into the wheat stubble. I put one bag of compound fertilizer in the row at planting for each mu, and when the corn is knee-high I spread 50 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice: once right after planting if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels are coming out. I spray twice for worms. Last year I got 600 jin per mu, and the year before I got 700, so I think 650 jin is a safe number to count on.

The stevia is on 0.7 mu. I rotary-till that small patch myself with the hand tractor. I plant cuttings I saved from last year — they are the traditional kind, not those new fancy ones the dealer tries to push. I put one full bag of compound fertilizer on that whole patch, and later I add half a bag of urea. I water it four times through the hot months with the well pump. I spray three times when I see bugs chewing the leaves. I hope for 250 jin of dried leaves. It is a cash crop, so I spend a bit more care on it.

I watch what my neighbors do. If Old Zhang puts on 50 jin of urea, I put on 50 jin too. When I am unsure, I do what I did the year before. Change is risky, and at 72 years old I cannot afford to gamble with the land that feeds us.
